_about: Flexible nasopharyngoscopy route through the LEFT nasal passage, computed by tools/scope_path.py (centred between the walls of the model's airway meshes; 1 mm between points, metres, Y-up). palate_offset opens the velopharyngeal port as in quiet nasal breathing: in the model at rest the soft palate lies about 2 mm from the posterior wall.

regions.name: Nasal vestibule
regions.teach: Skin-lined entrance inside the nostril. Advance along the floor of the nose, not up toward the nasal bridge: the floor runs straight back, parallel to the hard palate.

regions.name: Nasal cavity, along the floor
regions.teach: The scope runs between the septum medially and the inferior turbinate laterally. The middle turbinate hangs above; the middle meatus beneath it receives the frontal, maxillary and anterior ethmoid drainage.

regions.name: Choana
regions.teach: The posterior nasal aperture, bounded medially by the back edge of the vomer. The posterior ends of the turbinates are seen as the scope leaves the nasal cavity.

regions.name: Nasopharynx
regions.teach: Inspect the lateral wall for the torus tubarius and the opening of the auditory tube, and the pharyngeal recess (fossa of Rosenmüller) behind it. Adenoid tissue sits on the roof and posterior wall.

regions.name: Velopharyngeal port
regions.teach: The scope tip is angled down behind the free edge of the soft palate. Asking the patient to breathe through the nose drops the palate forward and opens this passage.

regions.name: Oropharynx
regions.teach: Posterior pharyngeal wall behind, base of tongue and palatine tonsils in front and to the sides. The epiglottis comes into view below.

regions.name: Hypopharynx, above the laryngeal inlet
regions.teach: The view down onto the larynx: epiglottis in front, aryepiglottic folds running back to the arytenoids, the piriform fossae on each side and the valleculae in front of the epiglottis.

anchors.name: Nasal septum
anchors.note: Medial wall: septal cartilage in front, perpendicular plate of the ethmoid above and vomer behind.

anchors.name: Inferior turbinate
anchors.note: A separate bone on the lateral wall. The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus beneath it.

anchors.name: Middle turbinate
anchors.note: Part of the ethmoid. The middle meatus under it drains the frontal, maxillary and anterior ethmoid sinuses.

anchors.name: Posterior edge of the septum (vomer)
anchors.note: The free posterior border of the vomer divides the two choanae.

anchors.name: Lateral nasopharyngeal wall (torus tubarius)
anchors.note: The auditory tube opens on this wall, its cartilage raising the torus tubarius; the pharyngeal recess (fossa of Rosenmüller), the commonest origin of nasopharyngeal carcinoma, lies just behind it. This model's wall is smooth, so the tag marks the position only.

anchors.name: Roof and posterior wall (adenoid pad)
anchors.note: The pharyngeal tonsil sits here: prominent in children, usually atrophied in adults.

anchors.name: Soft palate, nasal surface
anchors.note: Seen from above as the floor of the nasopharynx. It rises to close the port during swallowing and speech.

anchors.name: Uvula
anchors.note: Midline free edge of the soft palate.

anchors.name: Posterior pharyngeal wall
anchors.note: Mucosa over the constrictors and prevertebral fascia.

anchors.name: Lateral oropharyngeal wall (tonsillar fossa)
anchors.note: The palatine tonsil sits in the fossa between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches. This model's wall is smooth, so the tag marks the position only.

anchors.name: Base of tongue
anchors.note: Posterior third of the tongue with the lingual tonsil, running down to the valleculae.

anchors.name: Epiglottis
anchors.note: Leaf-shaped elastic cartilage. Its lingual surface faces the tongue base, its laryngeal surface the airway.

anchors.name: Vallecula
anchors.note: The pocket between the base of the tongue and the epiglottis, on each side of the median glosso-epiglottic fold.

anchors.name: Aryepiglottic fold
anchors.note: Runs from the side of the epiglottis to the arytenoid and forms the rim of the laryngeal inlet.

anchors.name: Arytenoid
anchors.note: The arytenoid cartilages move the vocal folds. Watch them abduct on sniffing and adduct on phonation.

anchors.name: Piriform fossa
anchors.note: The recess lateral to the aryepiglottic fold. The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve runs under its mucosa.
